scope: Read-only device headroom investigation; no service/process mutation, update or inference performed.

evaluation_workers.action: Wait for the currently running offline checks to finish; do not terminate them.

excluded_processes: Active Code/Codex, GNOME desktop, robot/device utilities and remote access processes were not considered for termination. The numerous Python processes outside the repository belong to nvpmodel_indicator.py, not evaluation orphans.
proposed_preparation: After the current offline checks exit, remeasure available RAM before making any other change.
If still needed and authorized by the parent, recheck fwupd Status=idle, Percentage=0, no pending systemd jobs and inactive refresh service immediately before a temporary stop.

Use the ordinary reversible service operation: /usr/bin/systemctl stop fwupd.service (via the normal authorized privilege mechanism). Do not disable or mask the service, alter timers, or change device settings.
Measure the real available RAM after the stop; keep all existing startup/runtime memory guards unchanged.
Restore the initially active service with /usr/bin/systemctl start fwupd.service in a finally/cleanup path, and record its resulting active/running state.
Avoid D-Bus queries while intentionally stopped because querying org.freedesktop.fwupd can automatically restart it; the refresh timer can also reactivate it.
limits: Measured fwupd resident memory is roughly 163 MiB, while the observed gate shortfall is roughly 183 MiB; stopping it alone is not guaranteed to satisfy the 2 GiB start gate or runtime floor. Offline checks currently account for roughly 80 MiB RSS, with shared-page/reclaim effects unmeasured. All values are snapshots and available RAM fluctuates.
authorization_note: This report proposes a temporary idle service stop only; it does not execute or grant authorization for that operation.
data_minimization: No credentials, environment contents or raw process command arguments were printed or saved.
